exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: An unencrypted update channel allows attackers to intercept and read update traffic through network sniffing.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted update channels can be leveraged to exfiltrate data over plaintext protocols without detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Without mutual TLS, attackers can impersonate clients or servers by forging or stealing certificates used for authentication.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Domain Controller Authentication
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing mutual TLS authentication enables adversaries to bypass or manipulate authentication mechanisms on managed components.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or deprecated TLS ciphers directly weaken the encryption protecting communications, enabling adversaries to decrypt traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Reduce Key Space
exploitedBy.relevance: Deprecated ciphers with reduced key space make brute-force or cryptanalytic attacks feasible against TLS-protected channels.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Encrypted Channel
exploitedBy.relevance: Replay attacks target the integrity and freshness of encrypted channel messages used for configuration updates.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Downgrade Attack
exploitedBy.relevance: Without payload integrity verification, attackers can tamper with or downgrade update payloads without detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DHCP Spoofing
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated source routing enables man-in-the-middle attacks via network spoofing techniques like DHCP spoofing.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Devices
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers can compromise network devices to manipulate unauthenticated update source routing paths.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated routing allows adversaries to bridge network boundaries and redirect update traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Service Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Without rate limiting, the update channel is vulnerable to service exhaustion floods that degrade availability.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Denial of Service
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of rate limiting enables network-level denial of service attacks against the update channel.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Root Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Bypassing certificate validation can be achieved by installing rogue root certificates on managed components.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Digital Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers can install malicious digital certificates to facilitate certificate validation bypass on managed components.
